dct_description_sm: 1) Assess the effects of observed pollutant levels on changes in vegetation community structure by comparing co- elemental concentrations in Hylocomium splendens with co-located surveys of lichen community structure to be conducted by the Terrestrial Vegetation and Soils vital sign; 2) Calibrate elemental concentrations in Hylocomium splendens with concentrations in passive air sampler devices (PASD's) in order to be able to use moss concentrations as a surrogate for deposition of contaminants on the landscape; 3) Determine current levels and long term trends of total mercury concentrations in piscivorous freshwater fish (e.g., lake trout, northern pike and selected whitefish); 4) Determine if any changes are occurring in most sensitive aquatic macroinvertebrates (e.g., diatoms) as a function of changes in N, S; 5) Determine trends in selected Persistent Organic Pollutants in freshwater fish on a decadal basis; 6) Establish baseline and long-term framework for monitoring concentrations of airborne Pb, Zn, Cd, Cu, Cr, Hg, Al, B, Fe, ,Total S, Total N, NO-3 using the moss Hylocomium splendens as a passive sampler; 7) Monitor changes in deposition of Pb, Cd, and Zn along the Red Dog Haul Road in CAKR and link deposition levels with changes in sensitive nonvascular plant communities via the Terrestrial Vegetation and Soils vital sign; 8) Monitor changes in heavy metals, S and N in streams, lakes and lagoons via aquatic vital signs.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Environment surveillance
dct_title_s: Wet and Dry deposition: National Park Service Alaska Region Inventory & Monitoring Program
